posts.cooked:
fjur:

posts.name: WalkingTarget
posts.cooked:
I keep up on a lot fewer webcomics now than I used to. I still regularly keep up on The Order of the Stick, xkcd, Penny Arcade, Goblins, and Dresden Codak. Only xkcd and PA keep anything like a regular update schedule, though.

fjur’s Questions of the Day #10: Which narrative genres do you prefer reading/watching/playing in/listening to?

posts.name: Dandolo
posts.cooked:
For me it varies by medium:

Movies: I’m a huge film fan and will watch and enjoy most genre’s but my all time favorite is Film Noir.
TV: Mostly I just watch anime at this point. My favorites are a mix of different genres, but Rom-coms tend to be the ones I look forward to most episode to episode.
Reading: The books that end up being my favorites tend to be existentialist or dystopian fiction but I find it hard to motivate myself to read those.
Games: JRPGs, plus everything made by Handleabra.
Podcasts: The only podcast I’ve stuck with for an extended period of time is The Letters Page.

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: I like most Speculative Fiction, I’m particular about Comedies and Reality TV, and I dislike Romances.

fjur’s Questions of the Day #22: If you could recommend one of GTG’s lesser known games, what would it be? (Here, I am defining “lesser known” as anything in the #other-games Forum category. So, pretty much anything but Spirit Island and Sentinel Comics things.)

posts.name: Jonas Ståleker
posts.cooked: Bottom of the 9th is pretty cool. Different. I always wanted to try Lazer Riderz and Galactic Strike Force!

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
Lazer Riders or Bottom of the 9th! Tactics is a lot of fun but has some issues that make it harder for me to recommend. Fate of the Elder Gods is a little too competitive for my tastes, personally, but it’s a good game.

(Galactic Strike Force has significant issues and I would never recommend it to anyone. Hopefully one day they come back around and give it the attention it needs, but right now it’s just not fun for me. )

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked: I got completely hooked on Bottom of the 9th after running demos for a day! For a game or two, it looked fun and amusing, but seeing game after game – and the range of situations that can happen – really convinced me how great it is. And it appeals to such a variety of people! I saw sports fans gravitate towards it, of course, but also people who got really into psyching each other out during the stare-down and people who tried to game out all the bonuses. For a two-player game, it also happens to work surprisingly well as a spectator sport!

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: Fate of the Elder Gods. (Sadly, it looks like GTG’s web-store no longer offers FotEG for sale. The above link is to its BoardGameGeek page.)
